questions.question: What is the graph's base node? (This decides token attribution and the sibling rule — structural vs. remembered-by-every-consumer.)

options.label: Collapse assistant by message.id
options.description: One node per assistant response (message.id); user_message/tool_result/passthrough stay 1:1; edges re-pointed onto the collapsed node. Tokens once, siblings structural. Loses intra-response block order (which is noise).

options.label: Raw record, 1:1
options.description: One node per normalizer event, faithful to the emitted stream, no collapse step. Consumers must re-apply first_block_of_message dedup and the no-sibling-edges rule everywhere, forever.

options.label: Two-layer (records + hypernodes)
options.description: Keep records as atoms AND add response/turn hypernodes over them. Maximal fidelity; carries the dedup trap in the atom layer and pays for two traversal levels.

questions.question: What are the graph's structural edges — and how do they survive Codex having no parent chain?

options.label: Portable relations
options.description: Containment + tool-pairing + spawn + agent-loop edge. parentUuid is Claude-adapter-internal only, used to recover response order; Codex uses stream order. Graph contract is vendor-neutral from day one.

options.label: parentUuid spine + synth for Codex
options.description: The parentUuid chain IS the graph; the Codex adapter fabricates a synthetic parent chain from stream order so both vendors look identical downstream. Simpler traversal, but bakes a Claude shape into the contract.

options.label: Claude-only v1, defer Codex
options.description: Build directly on parentUuid, ship a Claude-only graph now, revisit cross-vendor when Codex reader is actually built (currently deferred anyway).

# Plan: Causal Graph Design Doc

## Context
We've debated the causal-graph design over this session, grounded throughout on the real
normalized corpus (`traces/nrm_sess`, 9 sessions, up to 34 sub-sessions, 4,720 events).
The model and boundaries are settled. The user now wants a written architecture doc to
read and research before commenting — specifically with worked examples and back-of-envelope
math, and a real answer to the extensibility problem (the 7 known questions are a fraction
of the unknown question set).

Deliverable: one architecture doc via the `my-arch-doc` skill, written to
`docs/design/causal-graph-design.md`.

## Settled decisions (go into the doc as decided)
- Node model: Session ⊃ Turn ⊃ assistant[] ⊃ tool[]; spawn = tool + child_session_id ref.
- Turn is an explicit node. assistant collapsed per message.id (tokens = fb=true row).
  Thinking dropped (keep has_thinking). tools under one assistant = unordered set.
- Inputs: normalized JSONL (complete, build-whole-once) + OTEL (live, incremental per
  interaction span). OTEL spans map 1:1 to nodes. JSONL wins if both present (upstream picks).
- Graph is structure only. No rollups, no loop-detection, no source-selection — those are
  queries/upstream. resources[] = pointers to attachment events.
- Store: persistent JSON per session + in-memory build-your-own (no graph DB at this scale).
- No Claude session-end signal (grounded); OTEL flush is time/volume based.

## The doc's job (what's NEW here, beyond settled)
The extensibility answer = **hybrid query interface**:
- Tier 1 — domain API: named, typed queries for the known 7 (reliable, cheap, tested).
- Tier 2 — open traversal primitives: select / attr / children / neighbors / path /
  group_by / aggregate / resolve(cross-session). Composable. NLQ (LLM) composes these to
  answer unknown questions without new code.
- Both over one graph, behind a Port (Ports & Adapters). Primitives shaped like
  node→filter→walk→collect so they map to Cypher → Neo4j migration is body-rewrite only.
- Doc must WORK EXAMPLES: express several of the 7 + 2 "unknown" questions in Tier-2
  primitives, to prove the primitive set is expressive enough.

# Event Messaging Library (`src/common/msging`)

**Status:** Implemented in `src/common/msging` — see that module's
[`README.md`](../../src/common/msging/README.md) for the as-built API, config and known
limitations. This document stays authoritative for *behaviour*; where the two disagree, the
code is what needs fixing.
**Scope:** The shared transport library between the collector (producer side) and the
ingest service (server side). It owns reliable at-least-once delivery of event envelopes
(system architecture §5) and the producer registration/auth handshake (§7.1, §18.1).
It does **not** own event semantics: payloads are opaque to this library.

---
